question: What is the main reason why health insurance is so important for patients?

options.A: To provide free salaries for healthcare workers
options.B: To protect people from high out-of-pocket medical costs
options.C: To generate profits for government agencies
options.D: To completely eliminate all illnesses in a population

explanation: You got this! Health insurance acts as a financial safety net so individuals don't face financial ruin when paying for unexpected medical care. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h1)

question: How do your regular monthly payments (premiums) help you during a major medical emergency?

options.A: It stops the disease from spreading to family members
options.B: It guarantees immediate discharge from the hospital
options.C: It draws from a shared pool to pay for expensive treatments
options.D: It doubles the amount of medicine the doctor can prescribe

explanation: Spot on! Contributions from many people create a shared financial pool used to pay for individual medical care when emergencies happen. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h1)

question: Where does a National Health Insurance Scheme usually get most of its money from?

options.A: Direct cash payments at hospital front desks

explanation: That's correct! National schemes rely on public funds like taxes and mandatory employee contributions to make sure care stays available for everyone. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h2)

question: What is the main goal of setting up a national health insurance program?

options.A: To replace all doctors with automated medical software
options.B: To achieve nationwide access to healthcare for all citizens
options.C: To restrict healthcare services to high-income earners
options.D: To make public hospitals entirely self-funding

explanation: Well done! National schemes are designed to give every citizen, especially vulnerable groups, fair and easy access to essential medical services. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h2)

question: Which group benefits the most from Community-Based Health Insurance (CBHI) schemes?
explanation: You nailed it! CBHI schemes are built specifically for grassroots communities and informal workers who don't have company-paid or national payroll insurance. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h3)

question: Why do state or regional health schemes often exist alongside a national scheme?

options.A: To address local health priorities and specific regional demographics
options.B: To compete directly with private international clinics
options.C: To prevent rural residents from visiting city hospitals
options.D: To collect extra taxes without government approval

explanation: Correct! State schemes let local governments customize health packages to fit the unique cultural and financial needs of their own people. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h3)

question: How do private health insurance companies usually decide how much you will pay for your monthly premium?

options.A: Based on the current weather and seasonal changes
options.B: Based on the patient's favorite recreational activities
options.C: Based on the total population size of the country
options.D: Based on age, medical history, and lifestyle risks

explanation: That's right! Private insurers look at your health history and risks to set prices, meaning older individuals or those with ongoing conditions often pay a bit more. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h4)

question: What is a major feature of employer-sponsored health insurance?

options.A: It forbids patients from seeing private medical doctors
options.B: It is completely managed by the Ministry of Health
options.C: It is strictly limited to retired civil servants
options.D: It is provided by companies as part of worker compensation

explanation: Spot on! Employer-sponsored plans are job benefits where companies help cover or fully pay health insurance for their staff. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h4)

question: In a risk pool, what happens to the money paid by members who stay completely healthy?

options.A: Their unused contributions help pay for the medical care of sick members
options.B: The insurance scheme is forced to shut down immediately
options.C: Their money is refunded in cash at the end of every month
options.D: They are penalized with higher premium rates next year

explanation: Great job! Risk pooling works because the contributions of healthy members cover the costs of those who fall ill, balancing everything out. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why is risk pooling so important for making healthcare affordable?

options.A: It ensures that sick individuals do not bear the full financial burden alone
options.B: It allows hospitals to buy medical equipment without paying taxes
options.C: It guarantees that doctors receive higher salaries every year
options.D: It stops insurance companies from hiring administrative staff

explanation: Spot on! Spreading financial risk across a big group makes healthcare costs manageable instead of wiping out a single patient's savings. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h5)

question: Which of these is a common task for a nurse when dealing with patient insurance?

options.A: Checking patient insurance status and benefit eligibility
options.B: Auditing the financial profits of private hospitals
options.C: Setting the monthly premium rates for insurance companies
options.D: Designing government tax policies for healthcare funding

explanation: You got it! Nurses often check a patient's coverage to make sure treatments are approved and covered by their health scheme. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h6)

question: A patient is confused about whether their health insurance covers their prescribed drugs. What should you as a nurse do?

options.A: Advise the patient to immediately cancel their insurance policy
options.B: Tell the patient to pay cash and stop asking questions
options.C: Help clarify policy benefits and guide the patient through coverage details
options.D: Prescribe a different, cheaper medication without consulting the doctor

explanation: Wonderful! As a patient advocate, you help guide patients through their insurance benefits so they avoid unexpected out-of-pocket bills. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h6)
